newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Globus suspended after subsidy hike news.
newsitem.headline: Globus suspended after subsidy hike news.

text.p: The share price of Hungarian canned food maker Globus Rt jumped 20 percent on Monday, triggering a suspension of its trading for the day, after news that the government had restored subsidies on its canned goulash exports.
"Last year, canned goulash soup was removed from the basket of goods whose exports were subsidised," Globus chief executive Miklos Olah told Reuters.
"This subsidy has now been restored, ensuring that a characteristically Hungarian product can re-enter world markets."
The subsidy change took place as of January 1, he said, but had not received wide publicity until a radio show last Saturday.
Globus rose 400 forints to 2,150, a new record, before the Budapest Stock Exchange suspended its trading due to too rapid intraday rise.
Olah said Globus expected that the subsidy change would increase its 1997 turnover by between 200 million and 400 million forints ($1.2-$2.4 million), and its profits by a couple of million forints.
He declined to disclose the company's 1997 financial targets.
In the first half of 1996, Globus had operating profits of 113.5 million forints and net profits of 111.6 million on net sales of 2.37 billion.
The target for the whole of 1996 is pre-tax profits of 163.7 million forints on revenues of 5.6 billion.
-- Blaise Szolgyemy, Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 40 40 ($ = 169.2 Hungarian Forints)
